ES.d: Discount rate for every cash flow; rising real yields compress multiples before they dent earnings.
Index EPS is top-heavy — margin direction at a handful of megacaps outweighs the median company.
Spreads and the dollar tighten or loosen conditions faster than policy does; equities follow conditions, not the funds rate.
Payrolls, ISM and claims decide whether a slowdown is priced as disinflation or as a profits recession.
Buybacks, vol-control and dealer gamma set the path between catalysts and explain drift that has no news attached.

NQ.d: Cash flows sit further out than ES, so the same yield move hits harder — the ES/NQ spread is a rates trade.
Hyperscaler spending is now a swing factor for revenue and, through depreciation, for forward margins.
Inventory correction or a controls change repriced the complex several times; it transmits straight to the index.
A handful of names carry the weight, so single-stock news is index news in a way it is not for ES.
Roughly half of revenue is foreign; a strong dollar is a translation headwind on top of a demand one.

NKD.d: A weaker yen flatters exporter earnings in yen terms — the index and the currency are close to the same trade.
Normalisation lifts the yen and the discount rate at once, which is why policy meetings dominate.
TSE pressure on sub-1x book companies has been a persistent domestic bid independent of earnings.
Heavy machinery, autos and semi equipment weight makes the index a levered read on the regional cycle.
Overseas money dominates the marginal trade; allocation shifts move it more than domestic funds do.

ZB.d: The long end trades the average expected policy rate, so it responds to the path years out, not the next meeting.
CPI and PCE set breakevens; the long bond carries the most duration and so the largest response per surprise.
Refunding announcements and auction tails move the long end independently of the Fed — issuance is the other half of the price.
QT, foreign demand and issuance duration decide how much extra yield the long end demands for uncertainty.
In equity drawdowns the bid appears regardless of fundamentals; the correlation with ES is the trade, and it is not stable.

ZN.t: Fed cuts priced in the belly
ZN.d: The ten-year sits where policy expectations and term premium meet — most Fed repricing lands here first.
Indirect bidder share and tails signal whether real money or dealers are absorbing supply.
The belly rallies on weak growth and sells off on sticky inflation; when both arrive the curve does the work.
Large yield moves force MBS hedgers to sell into weakness, amplifying the initial move.
ZN against ZB is a term-premium trade; against the front end it is a policy trade. Know which one you are in.

6E.d: Two-year spread explains most of the medium-term move; the level of either rate explains little.
German industrial data and PMIs decide whether the ECB can hold; the euro trades the divergence, not the absolute.
As a net energy importer the bloc's trade balance moves with gas prices — an energy shock is a euro shock.
BTP-Bund widening reintroduces redenomination risk premium that no rate differential explains.
EUR is over half of DXY, so it is often the passenger in a dollar move rather than the driver.

6J.d: The cleanest single explanator of USDJPY; the yen is the funding currency and the spread is the carry.
Pace of exit from yield control is the domestic swing factor and the source of gap risk.
MOF has acted at extremes; the asymmetry near prior intervention levels matters more than the fundamentals there.
Yen strengthens violently when funding trades unwind — it is a volatility hedge that pays when correlations break.
Japan imports nearly all its energy; a crude spike worsens the trade balance and weighs on the yen.

BTC.d: Daily creations and redemptions are now the most visible marginal buyer; flow direction leads price more than narrative does.
Trades as a long-duration risk asset — easing conditions have been the backdrop to every sustained advance.
Issuance halves on schedule; the effect is on the margin of new supply, not a mechanical price floor.
Custody rules, exchange enforcement and legislation change who is allowed to be a buyer.
Perp funding and open interest tell you how crowded the move is; liquidation cascades are the mechanism for most fast moves.

ETH.d: Most of the time ETH is a levered BTC position; the ratio is where anything ETH-specific actually shows up.
Burn against issuance decides whether supply grows; the staked share decides free float.
Rollups moved activity off the base layer, cutting fee revenue and complicating the burn story.
Whether staking is permitted inside a wrapper determines how much institutional demand can actually arrive.
Same mechanism as BTC but thinner — liquidation cascades travel further.

CL.d: Quota decisions and, more importantly, compliance set the marginal barrel; guidance moves price ahead of the barrels.
Weekly EIA builds and draws against seasonal norms are the highest-frequency read on whether the market is tight.
Chinese imports, US driving season and jet recovery decide the call on OPEC crude.
Rig counts, DUC inventory and capital discipline determine how quickly non-OPEC supply answers a price rally.
Hormuz, Russian export capacity and Middle East escalation add premium that decays fast when nothing happens.

NG.d: Heating and cooling degree days dominate — no other contract on the board is this directly a weather derivative.
The weekly EIA number against the seasonal band is the market's scorecard for surplus or deficit.
New trains structurally tighten domestic balances; an outage at a terminal is instantly bearish Henry Hub.
Much US supply is a by-product of oil drilling, so gas supply responds to crude economics, not gas prices.
Power burn is price-elastic at the margin, which puts a soft ceiling and floor on the range.

GC.d: The classic inverse relationship — gold pays no coupon, so the opportunity cost is the real rate.
Official sector accumulation has been large and price-insensitive, which changes the floor more than the ceiling.
Priced in dollars and bought globally; dollar strength is a headwind independent of rates.
Western investor flows have been the swing factor between official-sector-driven and investor-driven regimes.
Geopolitical escalation and fiscal stress bid gold on days when the rates story says otherwise.

SI.d: Roughly follows gold with more volatility; most silver moves are gold moves amplified, so start with the ratio.
Solar, electronics and brazing make about half of demand cyclical — the part gold does not have.
Mostly a by-product of copper, lead and zinc mining, so supply barely responds to the silver price.
Visible LBMA and COMEX inventories plus EFP dislocations flag physical tightness that price alone hides.
Same monetary channel as gold, but swamped by the industrial channel when the cycle turns.

HG.d: Construction and State Grid spending remain the largest single demand block; property starts are the leading read.
The classic cycle indicator — copper turns with the manufacturing cycle, which is why it is called Dr Copper.
Chilean and Peruvian grades, water constraints and permitting shocks tighten the concentrate market quickly.
LME, SHFE and COMEX stocks together are the cleanest tightness signal; regional divergence flags arbitrage, not shortage.
EVs, renewables and data centre power are a structural bid that shows up in forward curves before spot.

ZC.d: July pollination is the single highest-leverage window; a hot dry stretch then outweighs everything else in the year.
Monthly USDA revisions to yield and carryout are the scheduled repricing events.
Roughly a third of the US crop goes to ethanol, tying corn to gasoline cracks and blending policy.
Brazilian safrinha timing and Black Sea supply decide whether US corn wins the marginal cargo.
Cattle-on-feed and hog margins set the largest domestic use category and move slowly but persistently.

ZW.t: Black Sea supply and war risk
ZW.d: Russia and Ukraine dominate exportable surplus; corridor and infrastructure news moves price faster than any crop report.
Winterkill, spring dryness on the Plains and harvest rain in France or Australia each set separate quality premia.
Russian export taxes and Indian import or export bans redirect trade flows overnight.
Chinese reserves are not on the market; the ex-China number is the balance that actually prices.
Protein and milling quality separate the classes — the futures contract does not always trade the same wheat you think it does.

ZS.d: China buys the majority of traded beans; purchase pace and hog margins there set the tone.
December to February in Brazil and Argentina now matters more than the US season for global balances.
Renewable diesel demand for soybean oil has decoupled the products from the bean; the crush spread is the real trade.
The new-crop soy/corn ratio decides spring planting mix and hence the following year's balance.
Port queues, truck freight and the real determine how much Brazilian supply reaches the market and at what price.

SB.d: The largest exporter's fortnightly UNICA data on crush volume and sugar mix is the highest-frequency supply signal.
Mills switch between sugar and ethanol on relative economics, so crude and Brazilian fuel policy set the sugar supply.
Quota decisions can add or remove millions of tonnes from the export market with no crop change at all.
Second and third largest producers; rainfall determines the size of the Asian exportable surplus.
Mills sell in dollars and spend in reais — a weak real incentivises selling and caps rallies.

KC.d: June to August frost risk and flowering-period rainfall are the two windows that have produced every major spike.
Robusta supply sets the floor for blenders; a short Vietnamese crop pulls arabica up through substitution.
ICE certified inventory is the visible buffer — low and falling certifieds turn weather scares into squeezes.
Compliance requirements bifurcate the market into traceable and untraceable supply, widening differentials.
Producer selling responds to the real; container availability decides how fast physical actually moves.
